ai.description: This legless lizard reaches 40 cm in length. It is olive-brown with dark lateral stripes and a distinct fold of skin along its sides. It possesses movable eyelids and external ear openings.
ai.identificationRemarks: To distinguish *Dopasia gracilis* from similar Indian skinks, look for the distinct lateral fold running along the body, which is absent in true snakes and most lizards.
ai.habitat: The Burmese Glass Lizard inhabits moist deciduous forests, grasslands, and scrublands, typically ranging from lowlands up to elevations of approximately 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Burmese Glass Lizard is primarily diurnal and actively forages for insects and small invertebrates among leaf litter, often using its tail as a lure or distraction.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dopasia gracilis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–7 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatching usually observed between August and October.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dopasia gracilis* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the Eastern Himalayas and the hills of Assam, Manipur, and Mizoram, at elevations up to 2,000 meters.
